```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5
)
```

# 1. Import data

This file examines individuals with multiple records in the registry to help determine how repeated records should be handled when defining the final Aim 1 analytic sample.

No records are excluded or altered in this review.

All output is aggregated. Individual identifiers and individual-level records are not displayed in the knitted output.

```{r import-data}
# ============================================================
# FILE PATH — UPDATE BEFORE RUNNING ON THE REAL DATA
# ============================================================

data_file <- "data/raw/synthetic_data.csv"

# ============================================================
# IMPORT DATA
# ============================================================

dat <- read_csv(data_file)
```

# 2. Create date and calendar year variables

The variable `fecha_creacion_caso` contains the date of case creation as a character variable.

This section converts it to an R date and derives calendar year.

```{r create-date-year}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    fecha_creacion_date = parse_date(
      fecha_creacion_caso,
      format = "%d%b%Y",
      locale = locale("en")
    ),
    year = lubridate::year(fecha_creacion_date)
  )
```

# 3. Frequency of repeated records

This section summarizes how frequently individuals appear more than once in the registry.

No individual-level records are displayed.

## Summary of repeated records

```{r repeated-records-summary}
record_counts <- dat %>%
  count(id_persona, name = "n_records")

repeated_record_summary <- tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "Total records",
    "Unique individuals",
    "Individuals with >1 record",
    "Records belonging to individuals with >1 record",
    "Maximum records for one individual"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(dat),
    n_distinct(dat$id_persona),
    sum(record_counts$n_records > 1),
    sum(record_counts$n_records[record_counts$n_records > 1]),
    max(record_counts$n_records)
  )
)

kable(repeated_record_summary)
```

## Number of records per individual

```{r records-per-person}
record_counts %>%
  count(n_records, name = "n_individuals") %>%
  mutate(
    percent_individuals = round(
      100 * n_individuals / sum(n_individuals),
      1
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(n_records) %>%
  kable(
    col.names = c(
      "Number of records per individual",
      "Number of individuals",
      "Percent of individuals"
    )
  )
```

# 4. Compare repeated records within individuals

This section summarizes whether repeated records for the same individual differ in case creation date, age, IPD status, or establishment characteristics.

The record-level dataset is used only to calculate aggregate summaries and is not displayed.

```{r create-repeated-records, include=FALSE}
repeated_records <- dat %>%
  semi_join(
    record_counts %>% filter(n_records > 1),
    by = "id_persona"
  ) %>%
  arrange(id_persona, fecha_creacion_date)
```

```{r duplicate-patterns}
if (nrow(repeated_records) > 0) {

  duplicate_patterns <- repeated_records %>%
    group_by(id_persona) %>%
    summarise(
      n_records = n(),
      n_unique_dates = n_distinct(
        fecha_creacion_date,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      n_unique_ages = n_distinct(
        edad_ano_creacion_caso,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      n_unique_ipd_confirmed = n_distinct(
        ipd_cofirmado,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      n_unique_ipd_discarded = n_distinct(
        ipd_descartado,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      n_unique_establishment_levels = n_distinct(
        desc_nivel_estab_crea_caso,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      n_unique_establishment_types = n_distinct(
        desc_tipo_estab_crea_caso,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  duplicate_pattern_summary <- tibble(
    Characteristic = c(
      "Different case creation dates",
      "Different ages",
      "Different IPD confirmed status",
      "Different IPD discarded status",
      "Different establishment levels",
      "Different establishment types"
    ),
    N = c(
      sum(duplicate_patterns$n_unique_dates > 1),
      sum(duplicate_patterns$n_unique_ages > 1),
      sum(duplicate_patterns$n_unique_ipd_confirmed > 1),
      sum(duplicate_patterns$n_unique_ipd_discarded > 1),
      sum(duplicate_patterns$n_unique_establishment_levels > 1),
      sum(duplicate_patterns$n_unique_establishment_types > 1)
    )
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Percent = round(
        100 * N / nrow(duplicate_patterns),
        1
      )
    )

  kable(
    duplicate_pattern_summary,
    col.names = c(
      "Characteristic differing across records",
      "N",
      "Percent of individuals with repeated records"
    )
  )

} else {

  cat("No individuals with multiple records were identified.")

}
```

# 5. Time between repeated records

This section examines the amount of time between consecutive case creation dates among individuals with multiple records.

For individuals with more than two records, each interval between consecutive records is included.

```{r create-time-between, include=FALSE}
if (nrow(repeated_records) > 0) {

  time_between_records <- repeated_records %>%
    group_by(id_persona) %>%
    arrange(fecha_creacion_date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      days_since_previous_record = as.numeric(
        fecha_creacion_date - lag(fecha_creacion_date)
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(days_since_previous_record))

}
```

## Summary of time between records

```{r time-between-summary}
if (
  exists("time_between_records") &&
  nrow(time_between_records) > 0
) {

  time_between_records %>%
    summarise(
      n_intervals = n(),
      minimum_days = min(days_since_previous_record),
      median_days = median(days_since_previous_record),
      mean_days = round(
        mean(days_since_previous_record),
        1
      ),
      maximum_days = max(days_since_previous_record)
    ) %>%
    kable(
      col.names = c(
        "Number of intervals",
        "Minimum days",
        "Median days",
        "Mean days",
        "Maximum days"
      )
    )

} else {

  cat("No intervals between repeated records were identified.")

}
```

## Distribution of time between records

```{r time-between-categories}
if (
  exists("time_between_records") &&
  nrow(time_between_records) > 0
) {

  time_between_records %>%
    mutate(
      interval_category = case_when(
        days_since_previous_record == 0 ~ "Same day",
        between(days_since_previous_record, 1, 30) ~ "1-30 days",
        between(days_since_previous_record, 31, 180) ~ "31-180 days",
        between(days_since_previous_record, 181, 365) ~ "181-365 days",
        days_since_previous_record > 365 ~ ">365 days",
        TRUE ~ "Other"
      )
    ) %>%
    count(interval_category, name = "n_intervals") %>%
    mutate(
      percent = round(
        100 * n_intervals / sum(n_intervals),
        1
      )
    ) %>%
    kable(
      col.names = c(
        "Time between consecutive records",
        "Number of intervals",
        "Percent of intervals"
      )
    )

}
```

## Histogram of time between records

```{r time-between-histogram}
if (
  exists("time_between_records") &&
  nrow(time_between_records) > 0
) {

  ggplot(
    time_between_records,
    aes(x = days_since_previous_record)
  ) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
    labs(
      title = "Time Between Consecutive Records",
      x = "Days between consecutive records",
      y = "Number of intervals"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

}
```

# 6. IPD confirmation patterns across repeated records

This section examines whether IPD confirmation status changes across repeated records.

Records are ordered by case creation date within each individual.

These categories describe the observed registry pattern only and should not yet be interpreted as diagnostic pathways.

## Individuals with exactly two records

For individuals with exactly two records, this table summarizes IPD confirmation status at the first and second record.

```{r ipd-two-record-transitions}
if (nrow(repeated_records) > 0) {

  two_record_ipd <- repeated_records %>%
    group_by(id_persona) %>%
    filter(n() == 2) %>%
    arrange(fecha_creacion_date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    summarise(
      first_ipd = first(ipd_cofirmado),
      second_ipd = last(ipd_cofirmado),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      transition = paste(first_ipd, "→", second_ipd)
    )

  if (nrow(two_record_ipd) > 0) {

    two_record_ipd %>%
      count(transition, name = "n_individuals") %>%
      mutate(
        percent = round(
          100 * n_individuals / sum(n_individuals),
          1
        )
      ) %>%
      arrange(desc(n_individuals)) %>%
      kable(
        col.names = c(
          "IPD confirmation pattern",
          "Number of individuals",
          "Percent"
        )
      )

  } else {

    cat("No individuals with exactly two records were identified.")

  }

}
```

# 7. IPD confirmation patterns across all repeated individuals

This section summarizes IPD confirmation patterns using all records for each individual with repeated records.

The categories distinguish individuals who are never confirmed, always confirmed, become confirmed after an initial non-confirmed record, or have another/mixed pattern.

```{r ipd-all-record-patterns}
if (nrow(repeated_records) > 0) {

  ipd_patterns <- repeated_records %>%
    group_by(id_persona) %>%
    arrange(fecha_creacion_date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    summarise(
      n_records = n(),
      first_ipd = first(ipd_cofirmado),
      last_ipd = last(ipd_cofirmado),
      ever_yes = any(ipd_cofirmado == "SI", na.rm = TRUE),
      ever_no = any(ipd_cofirmado == "NO", na.rm = TRUE),
      all_yes = all(ipd_cofirmado == "SI"),
      all_no = all(ipd_cofirmado == "NO"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      ipd_pattern = case_when(
        all_no ~ "NO at all records",
        all_yes ~ "SI at all records",
        first_ipd == "NO" &
          ever_yes ~ "Initial NO, later SI",
        first_ipd == "SI" &
          ever_no ~ "Initial SI, later NO",
        TRUE ~ "Other/mixed pattern"
      )
    )

  ipd_patterns %>%
    count(ipd_pattern, name = "n_individuals") %>%
    mutate(
      percent = round(
        100 * n_individuals / sum(n_individuals),
        1
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(n_individuals)) %>%
    kable(
      col.names = c(
        "IPD confirmation pattern",
        "Number of individuals",
        "Percent"
      )
    )

}
```

# 8. IPD discard patterns across repeated records

This section provides the corresponding aggregate summary for `ipd_descartado`.

```{r ipd-discard-patterns}
if (nrow(repeated_records) > 0) {

  discard_patterns <- repeated_records %>%
    group_by(id_persona) %>%
    arrange(fecha_creacion_date, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    summarise(
      first_discarded = first(ipd_descartado),
      last_discarded = last(ipd_descartado),
      ever_yes = any(ipd_descartado == "SI", na.rm = TRUE),
      ever_no = any(ipd_descartado == "NO", na.rm = TRUE),
      all_yes = all(ipd_descartado == "SI"),
      all_no = all(ipd_descartado == "NO"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      discard_pattern = case_when(
        all_no ~ "NO at all records",
        all_yes ~ "SI at all records",
        first_discarded == "NO" &
          ever_yes ~ "Initial NO, later SI",
        first_discarded == "SI" &
          ever_no ~ "Initial SI, later NO",
        TRUE ~ "Other/mixed pattern"
      )
    )

  discard_patterns %>%
    count(discard_pattern, name = "n_individuals") %>%
    mutate(
      percent = round(
        100 * n_individuals / sum(n_individuals),
        1
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(n_individuals)) %>%
    kable(
      col.names = c(
        "IPD discarded pattern",
        "Number of individuals",
        "Percent"
      )
    )

}
```
